0.original: Alphinaud seems eager to review your journey thus far.

48.original: I'm sure the others will be along shortly. I do hope everyone has rested well.

49.original: Now that we have refreshed ourselves somewhat, let us consider all claimants as they currently stand.

50.original: Zoraal Ja and Koana have completed every feat thus far and hold five keystones apiece.

51.original: Wuk Lamat would be equal with them but for Bakool Ja Ja's thievery, which has left us one short.

52.original: That conniving braggart didn't so much as lift a finger for the Feat of Proof and wreaked havoc for the Feat of Ice. He can't have more than three keystones at most.

53.original: He may think he can simply steal what he needs to win, but he's sorely mistaken. I will be taking back what is mine─this I swear!

54.original: I fear that reclaiming your keystone may not be enough─that is, if Bakool Ja Ja's unleashing of Valigarmanda is any indication.

55.original: Using his lead, I anticipate that he will move to obtain the remaining keystones before disrupting his rivals' attempts.

56.original: We may all find ourselves being forced to take from one another.

57.original: I can't say I'd be comfortable with that.

58.original: But neither will I surrender my claim to the throne so easily. If it's for the sake of preserving the happiness of my people, I'll do what I must!

59.original: The last two keystones we require are those of the Lay of Repast and the Lay of the Brotherhood.

60.original: The former depicts the cessation of hostilities between the Mamool Ja and Xbr'aal in the forests of Yak T'el. Specifically near a village called Iq Br'aax.

61.original: That's where I was born, if you recall. I haven't been back there since Papa took me in when I was a baby.

62.original: Where the Lay of the Brotherhood takes place, however, is unclear. In the saga, it is said that a foreign explorer came seeking an audience with the Dawnservant...but little more than that.

63.original: Eorzea has a similar tale─the explorer Ketenramm befriended a two-headed king known as the Autarch before commencing his travels across Tural.

64.original: He journeyed here several times afterwards but was ultimately lost at sea. At least, that is the commonly held belief.

65.original: Your two-headed king certainly sounds like Papa. So this Ketenramm fellow must have come to Tuliyollal!

66.original: But if he indeed arrived some eighty years ago, the capital may not have been built yet. Vestiges of Yok Huy architecture notwithstanding.

68.original: Wait─you said “Autarch,” didn't you? Then Ketenramm must have met the Dawnservant in <hex:021A020203>Mamook<hex:021A020103>!

70.original: One of the grandest in Tural, once upon a time─and the seat of the Mamool Ja's homeland. It too lies in Yak T'el, not far from Iq Br'aax.

71.original: Then all things considered, Yak T'el seems the obvious choice for our next destination.

72.original: From here, the safest method of travel is by dirigible. We should make for the landing once our preparations are complete.

73.original: W-We're riding in one of Koana's balloons? ...They can't be any worse than ships, can they?

75.original: Yak T'el... Where the Yok Huy dreamt of the golden city...

76.original: Ready to leave when you are.

77.original: How exciting! The design of Turali dirigibles intrigues me. I must note how they perform compared to Eorzean airships...

78.original: For as much as I wish we could ignore him, Bakool Ja Ja is a real threat. We can't afford to let our guard down.

79.original: The next flight to Yak T'el will be leaving shortly. Passengers are asked to keep hands, legs, and luggage inside the dirigible at all times.

80.original: A-Are we sure that thing will stay in the air? ...All the way to Yak T'el!?

81.original: A-Are you ready!? Bags packed and, er, good-byes said!? There's no going back once we lift off!

82.original: N-Not that I'm nervous or anything. I'm just making sure that <hex:021A020203>you're<hex:021A020103> not nervous!

83.original: Oh, who am I kidding...my knees won't stop shaking. Hey, will you hold my hand? J-Just until I've settled my nerves.

87.original: You're the nicest person I've ever met, <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>. I'll try not to crush your hand...

88.original: That stick-in-the-mud!? He'd never let me live it down!

89.original: There she is! Third Promise, wait just a moment!

90.original: Mablu and Tobli! Of course, of course─I'll wait as long as you need!

91.original: Sorry to delay you, but we were able to discover the origin of Krile's earring!

93.original: You said before that it gained popularity in Yok Tural as a protective ward for travelers, correct?

94.original: That's right! We tracked down the elderly merchant to whom first sales are attributed.

95.original: According to him, the design imitates an accessory worn by a foreign mage he met at market some twenty years ago. Little did he know that charming taste of salt would prove to be a commercial triumph!

96.original: A foreign mage wearing this earring could only be Grandfather. Did the merchant happen to mention which market?

97.original: One in Yak T'el─to where it seems you are already bound.

98.original: What luck. Then I shall seek my next clue once we arrive.

99.original: Is it mere coincidence that brought my grandfather there? Or...

100.original: Yet another discovery to look forward to.

101.original: Thank you both for coming all this way.

102.original: Anything for the Third Promise! Good luck with the rest of the rite!

103.original: Th-Thanks! I won't let you down. I've just got to board this dirigible and...and I'm as good as there!

104.original: Last call for passengers to Yak T'el!

106.original: Yak T'el will test her mettle, without a doubt.

107.original: The next Dawnservant must be willing to bear the full weight of this nation's history...no matter how heavy it may be.

108.original: Would it <hex:021A020203>kill<hex:021A020103> Erenville to give me the benefit of the doubt? Or the benefit of a second chance?

109.original: I can hardly fathom how difficult travel must have been before the Second Promise introduced dirigibles. Can you imagine having to walk all this way?

110.original: Well, that journey was delightful. The wind was fair and the vessel hardly rocked at all.

111.original: Worry not─Krile and I will ensure our Promise doesn't wind up at the bottom of one of these cenotes.

112.original: With thicker vegetation comes reduced visibility. I advise you to keep someone in sight at all times.

113.original: See? No tumbles! ...Thanks to Krile and Alisaie, but it still counts.

114.original: For all of Erenville's insistence, I have yet to discover anything particularly blue about this forest.

115.original: Is that Iq Br'aax over there, I wonder?

116.original: Take care not to get separated. I'd hate to lose you to this rampant undergrowth.

118.original: Iq Br'aax is up ahead. Let's be on our way.

119.original: Hah! I've fallen into High Tide Harbor enough times to be a professional diver─there's no way I'd fall into something like <hex:021A020203>this<hex:021A020103> on accident!

120.original: Are all cenotes this deep, I wonder?

121.original: What's so blue about this forest? You'll see.

122.original: Just so you know, I shall be very cross if you push me.

123.original: Erenville was not exaggerating about the cenotes. It would be a grueling ordeal to climb out of one.

124.original: Well, thankfully we made it here without incident. Let's not dally any longer.
